document.title: Instruction to Nominate Four Terrorist Leaders for Listing by the UN 1267 Sanctions Committee (State 070339)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Haqqani History: Bin Ladin's Advocate Inside the Taliban
document.note: [Unclassified] The page gives no separate summary. Documents 6 and 7 together show that Haqqani leaders were already on the UN 1267 Committee list of individuals associated with bin Laden, the Taliban or al-Qaida, and subject to a travel ban, arms embargo and asset freeze. Those named include Jalaluddin, his sons Badruddin, Nasiruddin and Sirajuddin, and his brother Khalil Haqqani.

key_claims: The US nominated Nasiruddin Haqqani, Gul Agha Ishakzai and Amir Abdullah for UN 1267 listing in July 2010.
Nasiruddin Haqqani acts as emissary and fundraiser for the Haqqani Network, raising funds in the Gulf and UAE.
The Haqqani Network had three main funding sources as of mid-2007: Gulf donations, drug trafficking, and al-Qa'ida payments.
Gul Agha Ishakzai, a childhood friend of Mullah Omar, heads the Taliban's financial commission and was Omar's financial secretary.
Amir Abdullah serves as Mullah Berader's treasurer and hosts Taliban meetings at his Karachi residence.
Anwar al-Aulaqi played an operational role in the Christmas Day 2009 plot by instructing Abdulmutallab.
